sentences.text: With consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.

02. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/Insurance Company being aggrieved by the award dated 2.3.2020 passed in MACC No.266/2015 by the 7th Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Indore whereby a total sum of Rs.41,82,030/- has been awarded to the claimant/respondent No.1 by way of compensation.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 03. Short facts of the case are that on 27/11/20214 the respondent along with his friends were going by their safe side from Bhopal to Indore in Zylo vehicle bearing registration No.M.P. 13 MH 001.

As soon as they reached Pushpgiri Highway road Bhopal - Indore at that time the offending vehicle bearing registration No.M.P. 30 H 0034 being driven by respondent No.3, insured with appellant came rashly and negligently from behind and dashed the same against the vehicle of respondent No.1 as a result of which respondent No.1/claimant received grievous injuries and his left hand got dismembered (traumatic NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25457 2 MA-233-2021 amputation) at the spot itself.
He was taken to the Govt. Hospital for treatment.
The FIR with regard to the accident was lodged in police station - Sonkatch, District Dewas.

04. The claims tribunal after considering the evidence available on record concluded that the respondent No.1 suffered 65% functional disability with respect to loss of earning capacity and thus awarded an amount of Rs.41,82,030/- as compensation to the respondent.

04. Learned counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company submits that the claims tribunal has considered the loss of earning capacity of the respondent / claimant at 65% while the doctor Ashish Shri Ram General Insurance Co Ltd vs Archi Rathore on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22875668/

sentences.text: Malhotra has stated that the respondent No.1 has sustained 50% permanent disability which would be 15% with respect to his whole body.

He further refers to Exhibit P/22 which is the certificate of permanent disability and points out that in the said certificate the permanent disability has been stated to be 50% with respect to his left upper limb.
Thus he points out 50% disability in left upper limb cannot be treated as 65%.
The claims tribunal has erred in considering the same at 65% and consequently the amount of compensation has also been awarded on a very higher side.

He further specifically points out to the para 5 of the cross examination of Dr. Ashish Malhotra (PW.4.) and submits that the said doctor admitted that 50% permanent disability in the left hand of the appellant may be treated at 25%.

He thus prays for reducing the extent of permanent disability as assessed by the claims tribunal by considering it as 50% for left upper limb and consequently 25%
for the whole body.

06. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.1 / claimant submits that the nature of injury and resultant functional loss has to be considered while assessing permanent disability for loss of earning capacity.
He points out by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25457 3 MA-233-2021 referring to the documents on record that the accident occurred on 27/11/2014.

He was sitting in a four wheeler, truck bearing registration No.M.P. 30 H 0034 came and rammed into the vehicle of respondent No.1 because of which the left hand of respondent No.1 got dismembered (traumatic amputation) at the spot itself which was subsequently implanted by surgery.
However the hand has become totally disfunctional.
The claims tribunal considered this aspect of the matter in detail in para Nos. 16 to 20 of the impugned award.
It has particularly been considered by the claims tribunal that before the accident the respondent No.1 was working as a dance teacher and hand movements in dance are very significant.
Because of this reason functional disability by the claims tribunal has been considered at 65%, which is not in excess at all.

In support of his submission he relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in the case of Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar & Anr. , (2011) 1 SCC 343, Rahul Ganpatrao Sable V/s. Laxman Maruti Jadhav (dead) through Legal Representatives & Ors. (2023) 13 SCC 334 as well a s Mohd. Sabeer V/s.
Regional Manager, U.P. State Road Trans. Corpn. 2023 ACJ 1 and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

07. Considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
08.

On perusal of Exhibit P/19 it can be seen that the respondent No.1 received primary treatment at Sonkatch and came to Bombay Hopital, Indore with dressing on left arm amputated stump along with amputated part from left mid arm brought separately with cloth.
It has also been recorded in the history that amputated part and stump both are badly crushed with contaminated present.
This history recorded in Exhibit P/19 discharged summary speaks for itself.
09. The disability certificate Exhibit P/22 provides 50% permanent disability into left upper limb with paresthesia.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25457 4 MA-233-2021 10.
A close scrutiny of the statement of Dr. Ashish Malhotra (PW.4) would also provide that there is deformity in left hand after its implant.
There was lack of movement in the joints.

The left hand has Shri Ram General Insurance Co Ltd vs Archi Rathore on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22875668/
2 hardened and the appellant was not able to do any work from his left hand.

sentences.text: Now this state of his left hand has to be considered with respect to functional disability affecting his work.
The Insurance Company has not disputed that the respondent No.1 was working as dance teacher.
The claims tribunal has recorded elaborate findings with respect to the same in para 19 and 20 of its award.
Thus it is undeniable that movement of both hands is one of the most essential part of dance and even of a dance teacher instructing students who are learning dance.
Considering this the functional disability of the respondent No.1 because of condition of his left hand has rightly been assessed by the claims tribunal at 65%.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar & Anr.

(supra) has held in para 13 as under :-
"13.
Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."
11.

Similar issue was considered in the case of Rahul Ganpatrao Sable (supra) in which the Hon'ble Apex Court held in para 13 as under :-
"13.

The five injuries which are permanent in nature apparently make him unfit for any employment even though the disability may be 60% or 85%. The compression fractures of seven cervical vertebrae resulting into paraplegia and further loss of b l a d d e r f u n c t i o n m a k e i t a b s o l u t e l y N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-IND:25457 5 MA-233-2021 impossible for a person to work and be gainfully employed.
Considering the nature of disability, loss of income is, thus, held to be 100% and not 50% as held by the High Court."
12. As such in view of the above factual position as well as the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this Court does not find any infirmity in the conclusion drawn by the claims tribunal.
As such there is no occasion to interfere in the impugned award.
Accordingly, the present appeal stands dismissed.
No order as to costs.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
